title: Herdr Desktop sidebar — agents UX
brief: Redesign the Herdr Desktop left sidebar (Spaces + Agents) so it answers, in order: what needs me, what runs and how far, what finished unseen, what failed, where/which program, then model/context/cost; idle agents quiet; RefactorIA palette, AA contrast.

artboards.title: Inbox first
artboards.tradeoff: Fastest path to what needs you (pinned question + failures with actions); Spaces become a secondary compact list and the same session can appear twice (inbox + spaces)

artboards.title: Sessions as cards
artboards.tradeoff: Richest per-session detail (task, progress, subagent/job chips, meta) sorted by urgency; cards cost height so only ~5 active sessions fit before scrolling

artboards.title: Unified spaces tree
artboards.tradeoff: One list, no duplication: location is the structure and badges roll attention up; urgent items are not adjacent when they live on different machines, so the top strip must carry the jump

artboards.title: Sessions v2 · calm idle
artboards.tradeoff: Idle reads as a rich, recency-grouped timeline (two lines, program + machine glyphs) and the empty state becomes a calm today summary with a jump to the last result; two-line rows cost ~2x height, so 'Earlier today' collapses behind 'Show N more' and the sidebar scrolls sooner
